fail_closed_rules: Mineral safeguarding area coverage is a policy safeguard, not a planning refusal, mineral ownership right or proof that extraction is economically viable.
A mineral safeguarding area does not mean the mineral will be worked; it protects potential resources from avoidable sterilisation.
Planning Data showing zero mineral-safeguarding-area records is NO_DATA only and never proves absence of safeguarding.
A minerals plan allocation, preferred area or area of search is not planning permission, landowner consent or a quarry operating permit.
A current minerals plan, emerging minerals plan and historical minerals plan must remain temporally distinct.
Planning Data minerals-plan coverage is incomplete and must not override the authoritative adopted plan.
A minerals-plan boundary indicates plan geography, not the geometry of mineral resources, allocations, permissions or ownership.
Local Aggregate Assessments are annual evidence and monitoring documents, not site-specific approvals.
Aggregate landbanks are monitoring indicators and must not be converted into parcel-level likelihood of permission.
Ten-year aggregate sales averages are demand evidence, not guaranteed future extraction or sales.
Aggregate reserves figures are tied to permitted sites and reporting dates and do not establish unworked mineral value on a parcel.
Aggregate Working Party advice informs planning but is not a consent or statutory allocation by itself.
National aggregate survey statistics are national/sub-national aggregates and must not be downscaled into parcel probabilities.
Aggregate import and export flows do not establish a particular wharf, railhead or quarry's future throughput.
Marine-dredged aggregate supply is a distinct source and does not imply land-won mineral availability on a parcel.
Secondary and recycled aggregate capacity must not be merged with primary mineral reserves.
An Aggregates Levy rate is a fiscal parameter, not evidence of planning acceptability, mineral value or extraction viability.
A safeguarded wharf is protected for freight-handling capability; safeguarding is not planning permission for unrelated development.
A safeguarding direction requires referral/consultation and does not by itself determine the planning outcome.
Safeguarded-wharf boundaries and viability assessments must be taken from the applicable current direction/review, not historical maps.
Draft London Plan policy is emerging policy and must not be represented as adopted London Plan policy.
Waterborne freight capacity targets are strategic planning evidence, not guaranteed site throughput or commercial demand.
National planning policy for waste guides plan-making and decisions but does not grant an environmental permit or planning permission.
The waste hierarchy is a policy priority order, not a parcel-specific suitability score.
Waste-plan allocation or safeguarding is not an environmental permit, operator licence, title right or proof of available capacity.
Planning Data waste-plan coverage may be incomplete and must not replace the authoritative adopted waste plan.
A waste-plan boundary is plan geography and not the boundary of an individual waste facility or permit.
Planning Data development-plan zero records are NO_DATA only and do not prove absence of operative development-plan policy.
A permitted waste-site record means a regulatory permit exists for specified activities; it does not prove current operation, spare capacity or planning compliance in every respect.
An authorised landfill boundary is regulatory context and is not automatically identical to legal title, ownership or the full planning application boundary.
Historic landfill data indicate known historic landfill locations and may be incomplete; absence is not proof that no historical filling occurred.
A historic landfill has no current environmental permit in force; it must not be labelled an authorised operating landfill.
A landfill quarterly-summary record is date-specific and must not be treated as indefinitely current.
Waste Data Interrogator tonnages are operator-return data for a reporting year and must not be treated as real-time capacity.
Waste received and waste removed are different flows and must not be collapsed into a single throughput or capacity figure.
Commercial-confidentiality handling in Waste Data Interrogator means absence of site details can occur and must not be interpreted as absence of waste movement.
Hazardous Waste Interrogator data are high-level movement summaries and do not identify individual producer/site risk for a parcel.
Hazardous waste movement totals can include repeated movements of the same waste and must not be treated as unique waste generation.
An environmental permit application, standard rule or exemption is not planning permission.
A planning permission for a waste facility is not an environmental permit and the two regimes must remain separate.
Deposit-for-recovery suitability guidance is screening guidance; acceptance still depends on site-specific permit assessment.
An approved waste recovery plan does not guarantee that every proposed waste type will be accepted into a permit.
Landfill environmental risk assessment and monitoring requirements do not establish that a site is suitable for non-landfill development.
Operational, closed and aftercare landfill states must remain distinct.
Permit surrender is a regulatory status and does not by itself erase contamination, geotechnical or planning constraints.
Landfill aftercare monitoring duration and completion criteria are permit-specific and cannot be generalised to every site.
Landfill Tax is a fiscal charge on disposals and does not indicate planning status, environmental risk or landfill capacity.
Current Landfill Tax rates must be time-stamped and historical rates must not be back-applied.
Waste statistics for households, commercial/industrial, construction/demolition and total waste are different series and must not be merged without compatible definitions.
National waste statistics and infrastructure counts are contextual aggregates, not parcel-level demand or facility viability evidence.
Fly-tipping statistics, waste crime and permitted-facility data represent different phenomena and must not be conflated.
Proximity to a waste facility does not prove nuisance, contamination, planning refusal or available treatment capacity.
Proximity to a mineral resource does not prove sterilisation impact; the applicable safeguarding policy and proposal circumstances must be checked.
Mineral extraction, waste management, landfill permitting, waste planning and contaminated-land regimes remain separate unless an authoritative instrument links them.
